newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel condemns U.N. vote on Jerusalem building.
newsitem.headline: Israel condemns U.N. vote on Jerusalem building.

text.p: Israel condemned a resolution passed by a special session of the United Nations General Assembly on Friday demanding an immediate halt to the construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"We condemn the resolution as a manifestation of unconscionable onslaught on a perfectly innocent act by Israel," said David Bar-Illan, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's communications director.

A resolution passed by 134 votes to three, with 11 abstentions, also called for an end to all assistance to "illegal Israeli activities" in the occupied territories. The negative votes were cast by the United States, Israel and Micronesia.

"It is really a very sad commentary on the United Nations that at a time when there are genocidal wars in Africa, when 21 Arab dictatorships trample human rights and when assassinations and terrorism are sponsored by recognised governments, the only thing the U.N. can find to condemn as a danger to peace is a housing project within the munipcal boundaries of Jerusalem," Bar-Illan told Reuters.

The special session was the fourth debate by a U.N. body on Israel's decision last month to build 6,500 homes for Jews at a site between Jerusalem and Bethlehem called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic.

The resolution "condemns the construction by Israel, the occupying power, of a new settlement in Jabal Abu Ghneim". It demanded immediate and full cessation of the construction and of all other Israeli settlement activities.
